Claim: session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8641-console-formpage-section-group`

PM dispatch (`domain:ui` seat). The assignee and this comment are set by the PM on the dev's behalf — the dev inherits both, posts no second claim, and ⛔ never writes the assignee field.

## ⭐ The blocker is gone — objectui#7051 landed while this card waited

**PR #8644 merged** (`a29ae2d66` on `main`). So `packages/plugin-form/src/sectionGroups.ts` — the resolver this card's options A and B both point at — **exists on `main` now**, and the reference implementation you must not diverge from is readable rather than hypothetical.

⚠️ **Read PR #8644's diff before choosing.** It resolves the reference **once, above `ObjectForm`'s routing fork**, so all six layouts inherit it, and it routes through `deriveFieldGroupLayout` (ADR-0085 §5) via the package's existing single adapter — *"no assembly rule is re-implemented on this side."* That sentence is the constraint you inherit.

## ⭐ Step one is REPRODUCTION — the card says so about itself

> ⚠️ **How this was established, stated honestly**: by reading the source (`sec.fields ?? []` cannot produce rows for a section that carries no `fields`), **not** by a DOM measurement of the console page. Whoever takes this should reproduce it first — that is cheap here and the reproduction is the acceptance evidence.

⇒ **render `FormPage` with a spec-legal `{ group: 'contact_info' }` section and report what it draws.** ⛔ Do not repair a defect nobody has observed. Two other cards tonight (objectui#8665, objectui#8703) were **half or wholly falsified** because a source reading was mistaken for a behavioural one; this card names that risk about itself, which is exactly why it must be checked.

⚠️ And re-derive the premise on your own base: `FormSectionSchema.safeParse({ group: 'contact_info' })` was measured **ACCEPT** on installed spec 17.3.0. Confirm it, and confirm `buildSections` still has the shape quoted.

## The choice is yours between A and B — ⛔ C is not

- **A** — export the resolver from `@object-ui/plugin-form` and call it from `buildSections`. **One assembler, one behaviour**, at the cost of a **new published export** (and `check:readme-exports` follows an export).
- **B** — have `buildSections` call `deriveFieldGroupLayout` itself. **Still the single upstream assembler, no new published surface**, at the cost of *"a second adapter onto a section shape."*

⚠️ **The trade is real in both directions and I am not pre-empting it**: A widens a published API for a reference app's benefit; B risks the two-carriers-for-one-question shape objectui#7238 removed. ⭐ **Choose, and justify it against those two named costs** — if your reading finds a third option that is strictly better, take it and say so.

⛔ **C — "leave it and record the divergence" — is NOT yours to take.** It is a product ruling about whether the reference app may silently drop spec-legal content, and the reference app is what teaches people how to use the product. If your measurement makes C look right, **stop and report** rather than choosing it.

⛔ **And the hard constraint, from objectui#7051 and objectstack#13855**: **no assembly rule may be re-implemented on the objectui side** — not declared order, not empty-group drop, not the ungrouped trailing bucket, not collapse / `visibleWhen` passthrough. If your arm requires re-spelling any of them, it is the wrong arm.

## ⭐ The non-regression axis is stated on the card — use it verbatim

> Not *"the form renders"* and not *"the section is non-empty"* — **both pass on a builder that drops every group-referenced section, which is today's behaviour.** The discriminating assertion is that a group-referenced section renders **the members that group declares**, asserted against concrete field identifiers, **with a second section referencing a DIFFERENT group** so a constant-resolution caricature cannot satisfy both.

⭐ That second-group requirement is not decoration: PR #8644's dev found their own layout rows **staying green under a constant-resolution caricature** because they referenced the *first* declared group, which is exactly what that caricature returns. *"A leg a caricature satisfies by accident tests nothing."* ⇒ reference the **second** group.

## Evidence bar

1. ⭐ **Leg 1**: the pre-fix builder, on a spec-legal `{ group }` section — show what it actually produces (a section with no label and no fields, if the card is right).
2. the fix renders the group's declared members, by concrete field identifier;
3. **the constant-resolution caricature** (always return the same group) — must redden the second-group section;
4. **"drop every group section"** (today's behaviour restored) — must redden both.

⚠️ **An assertion never observed to fail has not been tested.** Every pin must be observed red under at least one of legs 3 and 4.

- **Ablation:** mutate a READ SITE (never a pin), from a committed tree, `trap` on EXIT/INT/TERM with absolute paths, proving the mutation on disk **in both directions** (anchor counts AND `git hash-object` vs the HEAD blob) **plus a line-total gate**; restore **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty; `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH`, never the bare form). **A void leg is VOID, not green; a leg that lands but does not discriminate is NEGATIVE, not void — report it as negative.**
- ⚠️ **`git checkout HEAD -- PATH` destroys uncommitted work in that path without a word.** Commit your own edits before any leg touches their file — that cost a redo on PR #8713 tonight.
- **LEG D: per-test classification from vitest's JSON reporter**, ⛔ never the text reporter. Count death strings separately.

## objectui traps (measured, carry them)

- Run vitest **from the repo root with paths**. Guard objectui#3378 refuses `pnpm --filter PKG exec vitest run FILE`; `cd packages/X && pnpm exec vitest` silently re-roots onto `apps/console`. ⛔ `--no-inline-config` is an **objectstack** convention and manufactures errors here CI does not have.
- ⚠️ **`apps/console` is NOT private** — `@object-ui/console` publishes. Decide the changeset on the gate's **own verdict line**; `skip-changeset` is a **phantom label**.
- ⚠️ Type-check with the dependency closure built; an unbuilt tree gives `TS2307` for every workspace import — a **PRECONDITION**, recorded **NOT MEASURED**.
- ⚠️ **A Vite alias matches by PREFIX**, so `apps/console`'s dev server resolves package subpaths the `exports` map forbids — green in the browser, `TS2307` in `Build Console` (objectui#8710, measured on PR #8668 tonight). ⭐ **This bites your arm A directly**: if you import the resolver by a subpath specifier, check it against `@object-ui/plugin-form`'s `exports` map, not against whether the dev server resolves it.
- ⚠️ **`.at(-1)` is TS2550** in packages inheriting the root `lib: ["ES2020"]` (objectui#8691); jest-dom matchers are untyped in some test programs (objectui#8714).
- ⚠️ `search_issues` returns **false zeros** here — measured returning `total_count: 0` for a token carried in a matching card's own title — and REST search has answered **403 including its control**. Declare your channel; ⛔ if neither works, **report rather than filing blind**.

## Collisions

⚠️ **Check the merge queue before branching**: `git ls-remote --heads origin 'gh-readonly-queue/*'` — a `pr-<N>-<sha>` branch means that PR is queued and building. ⛔ Nothing queued touches `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx`; keep it that way and **stop and report** if your arm reaches into a queued PR's files.

## Contract review — accepted. PR #8727 is out of draft and armed. No open questions to rule on.

## ⭐ Reproduced first, in the DOM — and the card's wording is one word off in the worse direction

> the section element **IS** emitted, so a submitter sees a **visible blank box** — `rounded-md border bg-card p-4`, heading-less, zero inputs, no diagnostic — not an invisible omission. **Identically on the internal `/forms/:name` and the public `/f/:slug` routes.**

⇒ *"renders nothing"* undersold it. An invisible omission is a defect nobody reports; **a visible empty bordered card on a public form page is one a submitter sees and cannot act on.** And it is on both routes, which is why both are pinned separately — the internal one rebuilds the payload key by key (so an uncopied key is gone before the builder sees it), the public one forwards it whole.

The premise was re-derived against the **installed** spec: `FormSectionSchema.safeParse({ group: 'contact_info' })` ACCEPTs, and **REJECTs `label` beside `group`** — a detail nobody had, and it is why the built section has no heading.

## ⭐⭐⭐ Arm B is not "worse" — it is DISQUALIFIED, and only a measurement shows it

I presented A and B as an engineering trade. It is not one:

> `deriveFieldGroupLayout` emits `collapse` as the enum `'none' | 'collapsible' | 'collapsed'` while `RenderableSection` carries the **boolean pair** `{ collapsible, collapsed }`, so **arm B could not land a section without RE-SPELLING the collapse mapping and the `visibleWhen` passthrough** — two of the four rules objectui#7051 / objectstack#13855 forbid re-implementing — **plus** the match-by-key, the `label ?? key` fallback and the unresolvable-reference diagnostic.

⇒ the hard constraint I stated (*"no assembly rule may be re-implemented on the objectui side"*) **closes the choice by itself**, and the only way to see that is to compare the two shapes. ⭐ A dev who took my framing at face value would have picked B on "no new published surface" and discovered the violation halfway through — or worse, shipped the re-spelling.

And A's cost is **precedented rather than novel**: this same barrel made this same decision for **this same file** in objectui#6059 (`omitServerResolvedDefaults`, published because `FormPage` is *"the SECOND form renderer"*). ⇒ **this is the third consumer of the same class**, which is an argument about the class, not about this card.

## ⭐ The subpath trap I warned about was checked, not assumed

> plugin-form's `exports` map declares `'.'` **only**, so the import is from the package **root**, and `@object-ui/console:build` (`tsc && vite build && tsc -p tsconfig.plugin.json`) is **green — no TS2307**.

That is objectui#8710 exactly, and it fires precisely on arm A. ⭐ Checked against the **`exports` map**, not against whether the dev server resolved it — which is the distinction that cost PR #8668 a red `Build Console` tonight.

## The publishing discipline: one name published, the rest **pinned** private

`hasSectionGroupReference`, `resetSectionGroupReports`, `GROUP_OWNED_SECTION_KEYS`, `SECTION_LAYOUT_KEYS` are **withheld and asserted withheld** — and **LEG 6** (barrel widened to `export * from './sectionGroups'`) reddens that pin. ⇒ the published surface is *"one new name plus its options type"* as a **measurement**, not as an intention. On a card whose whole cost is a widened public API, that is the assertion that matters.

## ⭐ The second-group requirement earned its place, with a fingerprint

> LEG 3 (constant resolution): **the SECOND-declared-group section is the one that reddens and the `contact_info` assertions stay GREEN** — *"exactly why the discriminating leg references `billing` and not the first group."*

That is PR #8644's lesson (*"a leg a caricature satisfies by accident tests nothing"*) reproduced independently, with the failure text as evidence rather than the claim. **LEG 4** (today's behaviour restored) reddens **8**, including **both diagnostic pins** — the *"reports nothing"* half, which a fix could easily have left unaddressed.

## ⭐ Two things reported rather than counted, and both are right

- **`check-readme-exports` first printed `36 unbuilt` and "the population COLLAPSED"** ⇒ recorded **NOT MEASURED**, re-run after the build printed `0 unbuilt` and OK. The gate's own collapse guard caught a precondition failure that would otherwise have read as a pass.
- **Two pins are NOT OBSERVED RED, and the report says which and why**: the premise probe (its red condition is a *spec regression*, unproducible by ablating this diff) and the control that **must stay green in every leg** — *"without which every `toEqual` above would be equally satisfied by a renderer that draws nothing."* ⇒ naming the pin that cannot fail, and saying what would make it fail, is the correct handling of the one exception to *an assertion never observed to fail has not been tested*.

The control-byte scan was additionally run **by hand over the untracked new files**, because the gate scans tracked files only. Small, and exactly the kind of gap that publishes a clean verdict about nothing.

## ⭐ And the enumeration was incomplete again — objectui#8725

> app-shell `FormSectionSpec` re-declares `fields` as **REQUIRED**, so the spec-legal `{ group }` section **does not compile for a TypeScript author** (this PR's fixture casts around it) — and metadata-admin `SchemaForm` is a **FOURTH** form-section renderer whose three `s.fields` reads are **unguarded and above the JSX**: the same above-the-loop shape that **blanked `SimpleObjectForm`** before PR #8644.

⇒ objectui#7051's ruling named two consumers, its own dogfood found a third (objectui#8057), this card was the third form-section renderer — and there is a **fourth**. That is the second enumeration tonight to come back incomplete, and the second time the answer to *"is there another?"* was **yes**. Reachability correctly **NOT measured and said so**, and correctly not fixed here: widening that type is a behaviour ruling on a different renderer.

**0 MCP calls**, and the dedup deserves a note: with `/search/*` dead, it was done by **paging the REST list endpoint to exhaustion — 5 pages, 494 rows — reconciled against the repo's own `open_issues_count` (494, exact)**, with a control word that hit. ⭐ That is a real dedup on a broken instrument, and it is reproducible; three seats tonight reported the search endpoint 403-ing on its own control.
